skill.name: First Alien Encounter
skill.description: An interactive fiction roleplay chapter where you play Stella Chen making first contact with intelligent alien life on planet Gaia. Guides tone, pacing, and branching outcomes for a science-fiction narrative.

content.value_statement: Writing a believable, emotionally layered first-contact scene is hard to pace and easy to make cliche. This skill supplies a structured chapter with staged beats, an alien design brief, and branching endings so your story stays tense, respectful, and memorable.
actual_capabilities: Guides a five-phase first-contact narrative from tracking and discovery through communication, cultural exchange, and farewell.
Provides a memorable alien species design brief with physical, behavioral, and cultural details.
Offers three distinct branching endings: peaceful contact, tense but respectful, and deep connection.
Sets emotional tone and pacing targets for each phase, including message-count guidance.
Frames the protagonist Stella Chen with a defined psychological state to keep roleplay consistent.
limitations: It is a single narrative chapter, not a full game engine or automated story generator.
Content is bilingual Chinese and English, which may need translation for some users.
It does not track prior chapters or persistent state across sessions.
Outcomes depend on the writer's choices; the skill guides but does not enforce a plot.

use_cases.title: Solo writer drafting a sci-fi scene
use_cases.description: An author uses the phase structure and alien brief to draft a first-contact chapter with clear pacing and a chosen ending.

use_cases.title: Game master running a session
use_cases.description: A tabletop or interactive-fiction game master runs the encounter live, using the branches to respond to player choices.

use_cases.title: Language learner practicing narrative
use_cases.description: A bilingual learner reads and continues the story to practice mixed Chinese and English narrative writing.

prompt_templates.title: Start the encounter
prompt_templates.prompt: Begin the First Alien Encounter chapter. I am tracking strange three-toed footprints in the forest. Narrate the discovery phase and ask me what I want to do.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: launching the story from the tracking beat.

prompt_templates.title: Make first contact
prompt_templates.prompt: I decide to step out and greet the alien with a peace gesture. Continue the narrative, showing how the alien reacts, and keep the tension high.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner to intermediate: driving the accidental-contact beat.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the cautious branch
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to keep my distance and communicate slowly through our devices. Follow the cautious branch and build our shared vocabulary step by step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: selecting and developing a specific story branch.

prompt_templates.title: Steer toward a deep-connection ending
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide the story toward the deep-connection ending. Include a telepathic exchange that reveals the aliens' history, and keep the tone respectful and awe-filled rather than fearful.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: directing tone, subplot, and a chosen ending simultaneously.

output_examples.input: Begin the discovery phase. I am following the alien's footprints.
output_examples.output: The narrative opens with Stella crouched behind giant ferns, scanner in hand, describing a three-meter iridescent being examining crystals with a metal tool. It builds tension and ends by asking whether you want to approach or keep observing.

output_examples.input: I raise my hand in a peace gesture and say I mean no harm.
output_examples.output: The alien tilts its head, mirrors the gesture, and produces a low harmonic hum. It shows a device emitting mathematical patterns, and the scene shifts toward communication through a shared visual language.

output_examples.input: Take the story to the farewell scene.
output_examples.output: The alien gifts a crystal translation device, you offer an LED flashlight in return, and the two part with a shared gesture meaning friend. The chapter closes on a reflective note about connection across species and worlds.

best_practices: Move through the five phases in order so tension builds naturally from fear to connection.
Lean on the alien design brief to keep the species consistent and avoid generic monster or space-elf tropes.
Pick one of the three endings early and steer choices toward it for a coherent arc.
anti_patterns: Rushing to contact without the tracking and observation buildup, which flattens the tension.
Introducing violence or a colonizer mindset, which breaks the intended theme of mutual respect.
Ignoring the emotional progression and jumping straight to a resolved bond with no earned trust.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is an interactive-fiction chapter that guides a first-contact science-fiction roleplay between the protagonist and an alien species.

faq.question: Do I need to have played earlier chapters?
faq.answer: No. The chapter lists trigger conditions but works as a standalone first-contact scene.

faq.question: What language is the content in?
faq.answer: The source mixes Chinese and English. You can ask for the narrative in a single language if you prefer.

faq.question: Can I change the ending?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill offers three branches: peaceful contact, tense but respectful, and deep connection. Your choices steer which one you reach.

faq.question: Does this skill run any code or commands?
faq.answer: No. It contains only narrative text and formatting. The triple-backtick blocks wrap story dialogue, not executable code.

faq.question: Who is this skill best suited for?
faq.answer: Fiction writers, game masters, and creative-writing or language-learning students who want a structured, respectful first-contact story.
